### [Our approach to EU text provenance rules](https://openai.com/index/eu-text-provenance)

**OpenAI** · 2026-10-05

OpenAI has outlined its technical strategy for complying with European Union regulations on text provenance and AI-generated content watermarking.

- Implementation of text watermarking algorithms to identify AI-generated content under EU provenance rules.
- Deployment of detection tooling to verify the presence of OpenAI-generated text signatures.
- Restricting initial access to provenance and detection tools exclusively to trusted researchers.

**Why it matters:** Understanding OpenAI's rollout strategy clarifies how developers and researchers will interface with EU-mandated AI text attribution and verification tools.

### [Quoting Felix Rieseberg](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Oct/5/felix-rieseberg/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-10-05

Anthropic updated Claude Cowork to move both model inference and sandbox execution from local user devices to cloud-hosted virtual machines.

- The original Cowork architecture ran cloud inference but executed tool calls inside a local Anthropic-provided VM.
- The updated architecture runs both inference and the VM execution in the cloud, assigning each session an isolated sandbox.
- Local file access is handled via tool calls executed by the desktop app only when the cloud VM requests specific local resources.
- The architecture shift eliminates local disk, battery, and performance overhead while allowing tasks to persist when laptops are closed or accessed via mobile devices.

**Why it matters:** Offloading execution to cloud sandboxes removes local hardware resource constraints and enables persistent, multi-device agentic workflows.

### [Qwen3.8 27B addition in words](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Oct/4/qwen38-addition-in-words/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-10-04

Simon Willison replicated an experiment testing LLM arithmetic in words using Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf on local hardware, comparing non-reasoning accuracy against reasoning-enabled performance.

- Tested Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf on a local DGX Spark hardware setup using Codex Remote (GPT-6 Astra) to automate the workflow.
- Without reasoning, accuracy was evaluated over 30 attempts per number-length pair, producing a degraded accuracy heatmap as number sizes grew.
- With reasoning enabled, the model correctly solved 167 out of 169 single-attempt addition tasks across large digit lengths.
- Reasoning traces show the model executing explicit step-by-step algorithms, such as right-to-left digit alignment and carry management.

**Why it matters:** Enabling test-time reasoning traces allows open-weight 27B parameter LLMs to reliably solve complex, multi-digit arithmetic tasks that fail under direct next-token generation.

`llms` `qwen` `llm-reasoning` `local-llms` `mathematics`
